newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-ROENICK ENDS HOLDOUT, SIGNS WITH COYOTES.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-ROENICK ENDS HOLDOUT, SIGNS WITH COYOTES.

text.p: Star centre Jeremy Roenick ended his lengthy holdout on Monday, signing a multi-year contract with the Phoenix Coyotes, the team announced.
Roenick, a four-time NHL All-Star and twice a 50-goal scorer for the Chicago Blackhawks, is expected to play for his new club against the Edmonton Oilers Monday night.

The Coyotes, formerly the Winnipeg Jets, did not disclose the terms of the deal. But the Arizona Republic/Phoenix Gazette reported Monday that it would be a four or five-year contract worth at least $3.5 million a season, plus bonuses and incentives.

Roenick, 26, had been holding out for two months after being unable to reach a deal with the Blackhawks. The Coyotes acquired him from Chicago on August 16 for centre Alexei Zhamnov, promising winger Craig Mills and a 1997 first-round draft pick.

"Since the end of last season, we have ... added many important pieces to the Phoenix Coyotes, both on and off the ice," said Coyotes executive vice president of hockey operations Bobby Smith. "Jeremy Roenick represents a major piece in the building of an elite NHL team."
Roenick is coming off a sub-par season in which he had 32 goals and 35 assists, but was still Chicago's second leading scorer.
He became the first Blackhawks player to score more than 100 points in three consecutive seasons, beginning with the 1991-92 campaign in which he scored a career-best 53 goals.
Roenick refused to join his new team while Coyotes' representatives and his agent remained far apart in contract negotiations.

Coyotes star left wing Keith Tkachuk correctly suggested last week that negotiations with Roenick would heat up after Phoenix centre Cliff Ronning was sidelined indefinitely with a fractured right hand.
